name: kb_379_Normalized

schema.description: Represents a Glusterfs mount that lasts the lifetime of a pod. Glusterfs volumes do not support ownership management or SELinux relabeling.

endpoints.description: EndpointsName is the endpoint name that details Glusterfs topology. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/glusterfs/README.md#create-a-pod

endpointsNamespace.description: EndpointsNamespace is the namespace that contains Glusterfs endpoint. If this field is empty, the EndpointNamespace defaults to the same namespace as the bound PVC. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/glusterfs/README.md#create-a-pod

path.description: Path is the Glusterfs volume path. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/glusterfs/README.md#create-a-pod

readOnly.description: ReadOnly here will force the Glusterfs volume to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/glusterfs/README.md#create-a-pod

description:
The pod is configured to use a GlusterFS volume whose endpoint is **gluster‑cluster**, located in the **default** namespace. The volume source points to the path **/data/vol1** on the GlusterFS cluster.

The mount is provisioned with read‑write access (the `readOnly` flag is set to false), allowing the container to both read from and write to the filesystem during the pod’s lifetime.
